title: Tomorrow
verifiedBy: Claude Fable 5 — LLM review, authorised by repo owner

rules.text: Russian has two futures, and which one you get is decided by the VERB, not by what you mean. A verb of the everyday kind — the M4 kind — builds its future with буду plus the dictionary form: Завтра я буду работать. A verb of the finished-event kind — the M5 kind — has no буду future at all: its present-tense shape IS its future. Завтра я куплю хлеб is "tomorrow I will buy bread", with a form that looks like a present tense.

So буду is not "will". It is half of one of the two futures, and it never touches the other half: Я буду купить and Я буду пойти do not exist, in the way that "I will to buy" does not exist in English. If the verb is one of M5's finished-event pair, drop буду and use the verb alone.

буду · будете · будет is the same word as M5's был. Russian's "be" has a real past, a real future, and nothing at all in the present — that is the whole of it, and "Russian has no verb to be" was only ever true of the middle one.
Negation has not moved since M3: не goes in front of the finite verb, which in a буду future means in front of буду and never in front of the dictionary form. Завтра я не буду работать.

The present tense can also be a future when a time word makes it obvious — Завтра я работаю is ordinary Russian for a fixed arrangement, exactly as English says "I'm working tomorrow". It is not taught as a pattern here, but it is worth recognising.

words.note: Tomorrow. It opens the sentence, the way вчера did, and it anchors every line on this rung. Never changes shape.

sentences.trap: буду carries the future and работать stays in its dictionary shape — the same shape it had after хочу in M3. Only one verb in a Russian sentence ever takes an ending.
sentences.sound: ZAV-tra ya BOO-doo ra-BO-tat'. The в of завтра is said as an f, as it is in вчера and всегда.

variations.changed: swap the second verb — any of M3's or M4's dictionary shapes drops into the slot
не in front of буду, never in front of работать
буду → будете for the polite you, and the question adds nothing

mistake.why: Two verbs cannot both carry an ending. буду takes it; работать stays in its dictionary shape.

sentences.usage: Plans for tomorrow — the pattern you can build yourself out of anything M3 and M4 taught.
sentences.mnemonic: One ending per sentence. буду takes it, the other verb waits in its dictionary clothes.

words.cue: to rest · to relax · to be on holiday
words.note: One word for resting, relaxing and being on holiday — Russians отдыхают at the seaside for a fortnight and also for ten minutes on a bench. Pattern I: отдыхаю (I), отдыхаете (you, polite).

sentences.trap: English picks a different word for each size of rest — rest, relax, be on holiday. Russian uses this one for all three, so the sentence is vaguer than its English translations and that is not a problem.
sentences.sound: ZAV-tra ya BOO-doo ad-dy-KHAT'. Two unstressed о letters at the front of отдыхать, both flattened; the х near the end is the raspy one.

variations.cue: Tomorrow I will rest at home
variations.changed: M5's дома on the end — no preposition needed
the polite you-form of буду, and the time word moved to the end
не in front of буду, and завтра dropped altogether

mistake.why: A dictionary shape cannot stand alone as the sentence's verb. It needs буду in front of it, or an ending of its own.

sentences.usage: Weekends, holidays, and the answer to "what are you doing tomorrow?".
sentences.mnemonic: One Russian word covers every size of rest, from a bench to a fortnight.

sentences.cue: Tomorrow I will write a letter

words.note: "I will write" — and there is no буду anywhere. This is a finished-event verb, like M5's купить, so its present-looking shape is its future: напишу (I), напишете (you, polite). Its past is написал · написала. The на- on the front is what makes it the finished kind.

sentences.trap: Nothing in напишу looks like a future, and that is exactly the difficulty. The ending is the ordinary I-ending; the tense comes from which verb of the pair you chose, and this one has no present tense at all.
sentences.sound: ZAV-tra ya na-pee-SHOO pees'-MO. The ш is a hard sh, made with the tongue pulled back — harder than the English one.

variations.changed: the same verb in the past — the shape a man writes; a woman writes написала

variations.cue: Tomorrow I will write the newspaper
variations.changed: swap the object — and it bends, being feminine: газету
the polite you-form — still no буду in the sentence

mistake.why: буду belongs only with the everyday kind of verb. напишу is already the future all by itself.

sentences.usage: Promising to do one particular thing — the future Russians use most.
sentences.mnemonic: A finished-event verb has no present tense, so its present-shaped form is free to be the future.

words.cue: I will call · I will phone
words.note: "I will call", on the telephone. Another finished-event verb, so again no буду: позвоню (I), позвоните (you, polite). Its past is позвонил · позвонила. It shares a root with M1's Меня зовут — both are about calling, one on the phone and one by name.

sentences.trap: English needs something after "call" — call you, call back, give you a call. Russian is happy with the verb on its own, and adding a word for "you" here would need a shape this level has not taught.
sentences.sound: ZAV-tra ya pa-zva-NYOO. Three syllables before the stress, all light, then the weight lands right at the end.

variations.changed: the time word at the end instead of the front — both orders are ordinary
the same verb in the past, from a man — позвонила from a woman
the polite you-form, and still no буду anywhere

mistake.why: The same cross-wiring as S03. позвоню is the whole future; буду has no business in front of it.

sentences.usage: Arranging to be in touch — one of the most useful promises in the language.
sentences.mnemonic: If the verb is one of M5's finished-event kind, it does the future on its own.

sentences.cue: Tomorrow I will buy a present

words.note: A present. Masculine, and a thing rather than a creature, so it does not change as the object.

sentences.trap: куплю is M5's купил, one row and one word — the past and the future of the same verb, with no present tense in between. Tapping either shape opens the same note, and that is deliberate.
sentences.sound: ZAV-tra ya koo-PLYOO pa-DA-rak. куплю grows a л the way люблю does, and the stress moves onto it.

variations.changed: the same verb in the past — one word, two tenses, no present

variations.cue: Tomorrow I will buy a ticket
variations.changed: swap the thing bought — neither word around it moves

variations.cue: I want to buy a present
variations.changed: M3's frame — after хочу the verb goes back to its dictionary shape, купить

mistake.why: куплю is already the future. буду goes only with the everyday kind of verb, and this is not one.

sentences.usage: Shopping plans, birthdays, and anything you intend to get done once.
sentences.mnemonic: One row, two tenses, and the empty space between them is the present.

words.note: An exam. Masculine, and borrowed — the з is said as a z and the whole word is close enough to English to be free.

sentences.trap: Two words, and both of them are nouns — no verb at all. The zero copula from M1 is still running, and a time word plus a noun is a complete Russian sentence about the future.
sentences.sound: ZAV-tra ek-ZA-myen. The э at the front is a plain open "e", the letter Russian keeps for exactly this job.

variations.cue: Tomorrow there will be an exam
variations.changed: будет spelled out — the same fact, with the future said rather than left to the time word
the past cannot be left out: был is obligatory where будет was optional

variations.cue: Tomorrow there is an exam in the morning
variations.changed: M4's time word on the end, and still no verb in the sentence

mistake.why: есть is not a present tense of "to be" — M1's rule holds. Завтра экзамен, or Завтра будет экзамен.

sentences.usage: Announcing what is happening — the shortest complete sentence about the future you can write.
sentences.mnemonic: In the present the verb is missing; in the future it is optional; in the past it is obligatory.

sentences.cue: Tomorrow I will read a lot

words.note: "A lot", covering English's much and many at once. It goes in front of the verb, in the same seat as M4's часто and всегда. In front of a noun it changes that noun's ending — a job this level does not teach — so here it only ever describes a verb.

sentences.trap: English splits much and many by whether you can count the thing. Russian does not split them at all, and много covers both.
sentences.sound: ZAV-tra ya BOO-doo MNO-ga chee-TAT'. The м and н at the start of много run together, and the final о flattens to "a".

variations.cue: Tomorrow I will work a lot
variations.changed: swap the second verb — много keeps its place in front of it
back to M4's present — много sits in exactly the same seat there

variations.display: Завтра я не буду много читать.
variations.cue: Tomorrow I will not read a lot
variations.changed: не in front of буду, and много stays where it was

mistake.why: Understandable, and it throws an odd emphasis onto много. It belongs in front of the verb it describes.

sentences.usage: Saying how much of something you will do — and много is the same word for countable and uncountable alike.
sentences.mnemonic: much and many are one word here, and it goes where часто goes.

sentences.cue: Tomorrow I will get up late

words.note: "I will get up" — the finished-event partner of M4's встаю, and a different word from it, not a different tense. встаю is what you do every morning; встану is what you will do once, tomorrow. Its past is встал · встала.
Late — the opposite of M4's рано, and it sits in the same place, after the verb. The д in the middle is not said: "POZ-na".

sentences.trap: M4's встаю and this встану differ by two letters and by everything else. One is a habit and has a present tense; the other is a single event and has none, which is why it can be a future.
sentences.sound: ZAV-tra ya FSTA-noo POZ-na. The д of поздно is dropped entirely, the way the т of часто nearly is.

variations.cue: Tomorrow I will get up early
variations.changed: swap the time word — M4's рано, in the same seat
M4's habit verb — every day, not tomorrow
the same finished-event verb in the past, from a man

mistake.why: встану is already the future. буду belongs with вставать, the habit verb — and even then it would say something else.

sentences.usage: Weekend plans — and the clearest side-by-side of the two halves of a verb pair.
sentences.mnemonic: Two verbs, two lives: one has a present and no future of its own, the other has a future and no present.

words.note: "You will come" — a finished-event verb, so no буду. придёте (you, polite), приду (I), придёт (he or she). The ё is written, as always in this course, and as always it carries the stress.

sentences.trap: It looks like a present tense and asks about tomorrow. By now that should be expected: with this half of a verb pair, the present-shaped ending is the only future there is.
sentences.sound: vy pree-DYO-tye ZAV-tra. The ё is stressed, as every ё is, so the middle of the word is where the weight lands.

variations.changed: the answer, in the I-form — приду, and the ё disappears when the stress moves
the he/she form, ё still in place

variations.cue: Will you come in the evening?
variations.changed: M4's time word instead of завтра — the question frame is unchanged

mistake.why: придёте is the whole future already. Two future markers in one sentence is one too many.

sentences.usage: Inviting somebody, or checking that they are coming — the most useful question on this rung.
sentences.mnemonic: ё is always stressed. When the stress leaves, so does the ё: придёте, but приду.

words.note: "Of course." Written with a ч and said with a ш — ka-NYESH-na — which is one of the few Russian words whose spelling and sound genuinely disagree. It is set off by a comma at the front of the sentence.

sentences.trap: The spelling lies. Almost every Russian word is said as it is written; this one, and a handful like it, are not, and no rule will help you — it has to be remembered.
sentences.sound: ka-NYESH-na ya BOO-doo ra-BO-tat'. The чн of конечно is said "shn", not "chn".

variations.changed: swap the promise — Конечно takes any statement after its comma
on its own, as a whole answer

variations.cue: Of course I will not work
variations.changed: не in front of буду, with Конечно untouched at the front

mistake.why: The comma is not optional in Russian: Конечно is set off from the sentence it introduces, always.

sentences.usage: Agreeing warmly — and it is one of the first words you will hear in reply to a request.
sentences.mnemonic: Written with ч, said with ш. There is no rule; there is only this word.

comprehensionPool.cue: Tomorrow I will buy a ticket
Anna will come in the evening
Tomorrow I will get up early
Tomorrow I will go home early
Will you buy a present tomorrow?
